en.heading: November: Library and Information Services Month
en.origin: Library and Information Services Month highlights the work of libraries and information centres in providing reliable material for lifelong learning, research and leisure in the Philippines. President Corazon Aquino signed Proclamation No. 837 on 19 November 1991, declaring November 1991 and every subsequent November a national month for library and information services. The decree assigned a leading role to the National Library and a committee of the then Presidential Commission on Culture and Arts. It differs from National Book Week even though both occur in November.
en.promoter: National Library and Presidential Commission on Culture and Arts Library and Information Services Committee are the institutions named or involved in the statutory Philippine programme and its public activities.
en.purpose: Encourage access to information, library services and opportunities for learning throughout life.

en.heading: November: Traditional and Alternative Health Month
en.origin: Traditional and Alternative Health Month encourages public awareness of approaches to care discussed under Philippine health policy and the need to evaluate their safety, evidence and availability. Republic Act No. 8423, the Traditional and Alternative Medicine Act of 1997, established an institutional policy framework and the Philippine Institute of Traditional and Alternative Health Care. Proclamation No. 698 of 19 August 2004 declared November Traditional and Alternative Health Month and assigned activities to that institute and the Department of Health; the 1997 law is a predecessor, not the month's own enactment.

en.purpose: Explain the policy history of traditional medicine and support evidence-informed, safe health decisions.

en.heading: November: Book Development Month moved from June in 2008
en.origin: Philippine Book Development Month supports book publishing, readership and cultural and educational access to printed and digital books. It is not identical to the seven-day National Book Week. Earlier year-specific June campaigns took place in 1997 and 1998. Proclamation No. 120 of 25 June 1999 then established June as an annual Book Development Month, linked to the 1995 Book Publishing Industry Development Act. Proclamation No. 1436 of 17 December 2007 moved the month from June to November starting in 2008, to improve student participation and align it with National Book Week on 24–30 November.

en.purpose: Promote Filipino publishing, reading, book access and participation in the national book sector.

it.origin: Il Mese dello sviluppo del libro filippino valorizza editoria, lettura e accesso ai libri stampati e digitali, ed è distinto dalla Settimana nazionale del libro di sette giorni. Campagne specifiche si svolsero a giugno nel 1997 e 1998. La Proclamazione n. 120 del 25 giugno 1999 istituì poi giugno ogni anno, richiamando la legge sull'editoria del 1995. La Proclamazione n. 1436 del 17 dicembre 2007 spostò il mese da giugno a novembre a partire dal 2008, per favorire gli studenti e allinearlo alla Settimana del libro del 24–30 novembre.

en.heading: 1–7 July: Philippine National Culture Consciousness Week
en.origin: National Culture Consciousness Week highlights Philippine cultural heritage, arts, writing and the varied customs of its communities within a national conversation about shared identity. Proclamation No. 1148 of 31 May 1973 designated 1–7 July of every year, referring to cultural preservation, national identity and the constitutional recognition of cultural communities. Memorandum Circular No. 644 of 25 June 1973 directed government offices and schools to organize cultural displays, exhibitions and educational visits during the first week.

en.heading: October: a whole month for Mindoro's tamaraw
en.origin: The Tamaraw Conservation Month focuses on protecting the tamaraw, Bubalus mindorensis, a small wild buffalo endemic to Mindoro in the Philippines and threatened by habitat loss and other pressures. Proclamation No. 273 of 14 October 2002 designated October of every year as a special month for conservation and protection of the tamaraw and its habitats in Mindoro. The provincial governments of Oriental and Occidental Mindoro lead implementation, with the environment department's Tamaraw Conservation Program coordinating; this month is distinct from generic global wildlife days.
en.promoter: Provincial governments of Oriental and Occidental Mindoro and Department of Environment and Natural Resources Tamaraw Conservation Program are the institutions named or involved in the statutory Philippine programme and its public activities.
en.purpose: Protect the tamaraw and its natural habitat by engaging the communities and institutions of Mindoro.
